(module scope)

Media conversion pipeline — mirrors the manual scripts in tasks/:

images (any format) → {base}-mozjpg-uncompressed.jpg (q100 — tasks/image/100) {base}-mozjpg-50.jpg (q50 — tasks/image/50) {base}-mozjpg-75.jpg (q75 — tasks/image/75) {base}-mozjpg3-MSSIM-tuned-kodak.jpg (q25 + blur — tasks/image/25) + a .webp sibling of every .jpg above (the runtime's if-exists /preload chain prefers them when present)

videos (any format) → {base}.mp4 (h264, tasks/video/transform.sh) {base}.webm (vp9+opus — first ) {base}.mp4-scaledown-2x.mp4 (h264, iw/2 — iw/4 for ≥4K) {base}.mp4-scaledown-2x.webm (vp9+opus scaled) {base}.mp4.jpg (first-frame poster) {base}.mp4.jpg-thumb.jpg (q25 + blur thumb) {base}.mp4-scaledown-2x.mp4.jpg (poster of the scaled video) {base}.mp4-scaledown-2x.mp4.jpg-thumb.jpg

Tool preference per the original scripts: ImageMagick convert + mozjpeg cjpeg when installed, ffmpeg fallback otherwise (always available). WebP/WebM are always ffmpeg (libwebp / libvpx-vp9) — light compression, and an output that lands >= its input is discarded so the jpg/mp4 original remains the served variant.

refreshWindowsPath

Merges the persisted Machine+User PATH from the Windows registry into process.env.PATH. winget/choco persist PATH updates to the registry on install, but a terminal (or IDE) spawned before the install keeps the stale snapshot — every spawn below inherits this process env, so refreshing here makes just-installed tools (ffmpeg, gcloud, …) discoverable within the same setup run. No-op off win32 and when PowerShell is unavailable.

imgMagick

ImageMagick invocation for the platform: magick convert … is the modern entrypoint on every OS and the only correct one on Windows — where bare convert is Microsoft's filesystem tool, never ImageMagick.

  • @param t Tool map from detectTools().
  • @param args Arguments for the convert subcommand.
  • @returns {Promise} resolves when the conversion exits 0.

imOk

True when an ImageMagick binary is usable on this platform.

(module scope)

(module scope)

Emits a compressed sibling only when it actually compresses — a webp/webm output that lands >= its source is deleted so the jpg/mp4 remains the variant the runtime serves ("leave them as they are" for non-compressible assets). Returns the kept basename or null.
